entities.name: Query protein 768 aa
observations: Sequence length is 768 aa; calculated molecular mass is 86.95 kDa and theoretical pI is 8.41.
Near-exact reviewed homologs identify the sequence as KCNH8, a voltage-gated delayed-rectifier potassium-channel alpha subunit.
Architecture includes an N-terminal PAS domain, a six-transmembrane ion-channel region with S1-S4 voltage sensor and S5-H5-S6 pore module, and a C-terminal cyclic-nucleotide-binding-like domain.
The protein is inferred to be a plasma-membrane multipass channel; exact localization and physiology depend on organism and experimental context.

entities.name: KCNH8
observations: Reviewed rat, mouse, and human homologs support a pore-forming alpha subunit of a voltage-gated delayed-rectifier potassium channel.
Reported channel behavior includes slowly activating, non-inactivating, slowly deactivating outward potassium currents; activation is strongly pH-dependent in the cited rat characterization.
The channel likely forms homo- or heterotetramers and can associate with modulating beta subunits.
Curated/localized as a multi-pass plasma-membrane protein.

entities.name: Potassium ion transport
observations: KCNH8 homolog annotations include potassium ion transmembrane transport, potassium ion transport, and regulation of membrane potential.

entities.name: Voltage-gated potassium channel activity
observations: KCNH8 homologs are annotated with voltage-gated potassium channel activity and delayed-rectifier potassium channel activity.
